newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan stocks seen rising once IMF deal unveiled.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan stocks seen rising once IMF deal unveiled.

text.p: A leading brokerage house said on Monday that Pakistani stocks could get a boost once the government announces an IMF-inspired reform package.

Carr Mashriq, local affiliate of W.I. Carr (Far East) Ltd, said the announcement of the reforms demanded by the International Monetary Fund could send the Karachi Stock Exchange 100-share index above 1,550 points.
Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government has apparently agreed to the IMF package, but has not disclosed its contents.
But the new measures, expected to slash spending and impose an agricultural income tax, are likely to be announced ahead of the arrival of an IMF review mission on Thursday.
"After the promulgation of the economic package we anticipate a rally back up to 1,550-point levels," said a research report of Carr Mashriq received by Reuters on Monday.
At the Karachi bourse, dealers waited anxiously for details of the new measures. The index was up 2.38 points, or 0.17 percent, at 1,369.98 at noon on settlement day short-covering.
"The government seems prepared to take some extremely unpopular measures like the levy of agriculture tax and reduction in government spending in order to appease the IMF," the report said.
Three provinces passed legislation in June 1994 to introduce the agriculture income tax, but provincial government officials say resistance from rich landowners has meant negligible receipts.
Populous Punjab province, Pakistan's leading agriculture producer, has not introduced the tax because of opposition from the landowners who dominate the provincial assembly.
Carr Mashriq said abolition of tax rebates and subsidies would lead to short-term pain but would help set the economy on the right course.
Pakistan, faced with a yawning current account deficit and shrinking foreign reserves, is under IMF pressure to reduce its budget deficit to four percent of gross domestic product.

"The market will not immediately rally to 1,800 or so, but will definitely find a higher minimum level as current valuations reflect all the bad news and do not factor in any improvement," Carr Mashriq said.
The IMF mission must complete a long-delayed review of the economy before the fund releases further tranches of a stalled $600 million standby loan.
The IMF withheld disbursements due in June and September because of dissatisfaction with Pakistan's economic policies and confusion surrounding the fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) budget.

"If we put the pieces together and try to make some sense of all the statements being given out by the government, it gets very clear that this time round the economic reform package will contain some tough choices," the Carr Mashriq report said.
It advised investors to buy Fauji Fertlizer, Hub Power Co, Sui Northern Gas, Sui Southern Gas, Engro Chemical and Pakistan State Oil.
"With a limited downside to the market, we feel that the IMF approval will have a positive effect on the index with our big six outperforming the KSE," the report added.
